title: Workflows: feature branch, trunk based and Git Flow

videos.script: Git does not tell a team how to work. It gives you branches and merges, and leaves the rest to you. {{nothing}} So every team ends up answering the same questions. How long does a branch live? When does work reach main? What exactly gets released, and how? {{questions}} The answers cluster into three shapes, and you will meet all three. {{three}} Feature branches. One branch per piece of work, reviewed in a pull request, merged when it is done. This is where most teams start. {{feature}} Trunk based. Branches so short they last hours, and unfinished work merged anyway, switched off until it is ready. {{trunk}} And Git Flow. A branch for development, a branch for releases, a branch for urgent fixes, each with its own rules. {{flow}} None of them is right in general. Each one fits a particular way of shipping software. By the end of this lesson, you will know which question to ask to choose. {{title}}
